title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

standard_code: Class 6, Curiosity Chapter 9: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
standard_text: Mixtures and the need to separate them; handpicking, threshing, winnowing, sieving, sedimentation, decantation, filtration, evaporation, condensation, churning and magnetic separation (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 9).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 9: handpicking, threshing, winnowing, sieving, sedimentation, decantation, filtration, evaporation, churning and using a magnet. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Choose the method that suits the mixture.
key_sub: Insoluble solids: filter. Dissolved salt: evaporate.
body_html:
How to think about it

A mixture can be separated in different ways. We handpick stones from rice, thresh stalks to get grain, winnow to blow away husk, sieve flour, churn curd to get butter and use a magnet to pick out iron.

Heavy insoluble particles settle in water (sedimentation) and the clear water is poured off (decantation); filtration removes finer particles. A dissolved substance such as salt passes through a filter, so we evaporate the water to get the salt and condense the vapour to get pure water.

Example

Salt and sand: first step?

only salt dissolves

Answer: add water and filter

Example

Iron filings in sand?

iron is magnetic

Answer: use a magnet

Common mistakes

  • Trying to filter out dissolved salt.
  • Mixing up sedimentation and decantation.
  • Thinking winnowing needs water.

faq.q: What is the difference between sedimentation and decantation?
faq.a: Sedimentation is the settling of heavy particles; decantation is pouring off the clear liquid above them.

faq.q: How do we get salt from sea water?
faq.a: Sea water is left in shallow pans; the Sun evaporates the water and the salt is left behind.
